results.name: Chair Pose
instructions: Stand upright with your feet shoulder width apart and raise both arms overhead with your palms facing each other.
Push your hips back and bend your knees to lower into a squat while keeping your chest lifted and your arms extended overhead.
Hold the position while keeping your heels on the floor, and your weight evenly distributed across both feet.
Press through your heels to return to the starting position with control and repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Sit your hips back as if lowering onto a chair.
Keep your knees aligned with your toes without allowing them to collapse inward.
Engage your core to improve balance and stability.
Inhale as you lower into the pose and exhale as you return to standing.
results.description: Chair Pose is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Hamstrings, Calves, Core.

results.name: Child Pose Arms Extended Left Right
instructions: Begin in a kneeling position with your hips resting on your heels, face forward with your hands to your sides.
Lower your torso toward the floor and slowly extend both hands to one side while keeping your hips resting on your heels, resting your forehead on your hands.
Hold the stretch when you feel it along the side of your upper back and torso.
Return your to your starting position, repeat the stretch to the opposite side, and continue alternating sides.
tips: Keep your hips resting on your heels throughout the stretch.
Keep your shoulders relaxed and avoid shrugging them toward your ears
Stretch only until you feel a comfortable pull along your side.
Inhale in the center and exhale as you reach to each side.
results.description: Child Pose Arms Extended Left Right is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders, Lower Back.

results.name: Child Pose Arms on Side
instructions: Begin in a tall kneeling position with your knees slightly apart and your hands resting by your sides.
Sit your hips back onto your heels as you lower your chest toward your thighs, allowing your forehead to rest on the floor.
Extend your arms alongside your body with your palms facing upward and relax your shoulders.
Hold the stretch, then slowly return to the starting position with control.
tips: Keep your hips resting on your heels throughout the stretch.
Allow your shoulders to relax completely as your arms rest beside your body.
Avoid lifting your hips away from your heels.
Inhale deeply and exhale as you settle further into the stretch.
results.description: Child Pose Arms on Side is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Glutes.

results.name: Child Pose Elbows on Block
instructions: Begin in a tall kneeling position with two yoga blocks placed in front of you. Rest both elbows on each block and bring your hands together behind your head.
Sit your hips back toward your heels as you lower your chest toward the floor.
Allow your elbows to remain on the block while gently sinking your chest to deepen the stretch through your shoulders and upper back.
Hold the stretch, then slowly return to the starting position with control.
tips: Keep your elbows supported on the block throughout the stretch.
Keep your hips moving toward your heels as you lower your chest.
Avoid rounding your lower back excessively.
Inhale before lowering and exhale as you deepen the stretch.
results.description: Child Pose Elbows on Block is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the delts (shoulders). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Chest, Upper Back, Lower Back.

results.name: Child Pose Up
instructions: Begin on all fours with your hands directly under your shoulders and your knees under your hips. Keep your elbows bent close to your body with chest close to the floor.
Push through your hands to lift your upper body slightly while simultaneously pushing your hips backwards towards your heels. Straighten your arms as you move your hips back.
Continue to push your hips back until they are close to your heels, extending your arms fully in front of you on the floor.
Hold this position for the desired duration, breathing deeply and allowing your body to relax into the stretch.
tips: Focus on pushing your hips back towards your heels to deepen the stretch in your lower back and shoulders.
Perform the movement slowly and with control to maximize the effectiveness of the stretch.
Breathe deeply and steadily, inhaling as you lift your upper body and exhaling as you push your hips back.
Use this pose to gently stretch and open up the muscles in your back, shoulders, and hips.
results.description: Child Pose Up is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Chest.

results.name: Child Pose
instructions: Begin by kneeling on the floor with your knees together or slightly apart, and your big toes touching.
Sit back on your heels, extending your arms forward on the floor, lowering your torso down between your thighs.
Rest your forehead on the floor, keeping your arms extended out in front of you with palms facing down.
Hold this position for the desired duration, breathing deeply and allowing your body to relax into the stretch.
tips: Focus on breathing deeply and steadily, inhaling through your nose and exhaling through your mouth.
Allow your hips to sink back towards your heels to deepen the stretch in your lower back and hips.
If needed, you can place a cushion or folded blanket between your thighs and calves for added comfort.
Keep your forehead resting on the floor or on a cushion to maintain a relaxed neck position.
Use this pose as a gentle way to release tension and stretch the muscles in your back, hips, and shoulders.
results.description: Child Pose is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Cobra Full Push Up
instructions: Begin in a plank position with your hands placed under your shoulders, your body forming a straight line from head to heels.
Perform a push-up by lowering your body towards the floor by bending your elbows, keeping them close to your sides.
As your chest reaches the floor, leave your hips on the floor and press through your palms to lift your chest up, straightening your arms and arching your back into the cobra position.
Bend your arms to lower your chest back to the floor, then press through your palms to lift your body back to the starting plank position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your chest, shoulders, and triceps to push your body up while keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Perform the movement with control, especially during the transitions between plank, push-up, and cobra positions to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Keep your hips on the floor during the cobra position to maintain proper form and maximize the stretch in your lower back.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and lift your chest, and inhaling as you lower yourself.
results.description: Cobra Full Push Up is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Lower Back.

results.name: Cobra Push Up
instructions: Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed at shoulder level, palms flat on the floor and elbows close to your sides.

Engage your core and press through your palms to lift your chest off the floor, straightening your arms to come into the cobra position. 3. Keep your hips on the floor. Hold the cobra position for a moment, feeling the stretch in your lower back and abdomen.
. Slowly lower your chest back to the floor by bending your elbows, returning to the starting position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your chest, shoulders, and triceps to push your body up while keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Keep your hips on the floor during the cobra position to maintain proper form and maximize the stretch in your lower back.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and lift your chest, and inhaling as you lower yourself.
results.description: Cobra Push Up is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Lower Back.

results.name: Cobra Side Ab Stretch
instructions: Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed at shoulder level, palms flat on the floor.
Press through your palms to lift your chest off the floor, straightening your arms to come into the cobra position, keeping your hips on the floor.

From the cobra position, slowly rotate your torso to the right, looking over your right shoulder, and hold the stretch for a moment, feeling the stretch along the left side of your abdomen. Return to the center cobra position.

Slowly rotate your torso to the left, looking over your left shoulder, and hold the stretch, feeling the stretch along the right side of your abdomen. Return to the center cobra position. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on using your chest, shoulders, and triceps to push your body up while keeping your elbows close to your sides.
Perform the movement with control to maximize muscle activation and prevent injury.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
Breathe steadily throughout the exercise, exhaling as you push up and lift your chest, and inhaling as you lower yourself and rotate.
Keep your hips on the floor during the cobra and side stretches to maintain proper form and maximize the stretch in your lower back and sides.
results.description: Cobra Side Ab Stretch is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Lower Back.

results.name: Cobra Yoga Pose Hold
instructions: Begin by lying face down on the floor with your legs extended straight behind you and your hands placed at shoulder level, palms flat on the floor.
Engage your core and press through your palms to lift your chest off the floor, straightening your arms to come into the cobra position, keeping your hips on the floor.
Hold the cobra position, keeping your arms straight and your chest lifted, while breathing steadily.
tips: Perform the movement with control, ensuring a smooth and steady rise into the cobra position.
Ensure your shoulders remain down and away from your ears to avoid unnecessary strain.
Breathe deeply and steadily throughout the exercise, inhaling as you lift your chest and exhaling as you hold the position.
Keep your hips on the floor during the cobra hold to maintain proper form and maximize the stretch in your lower back and abdomen.
results.description: Cobra Yoga Pose Hold is a beginner multi-joint compound static exercise targeting the pectorals (chest). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the yoga category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Lower Back.
